# entropy_src_core Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

The entropy source core collects raw entropy from one of two available source classes:

- an external true-random noise source, and
- an internal digital pseudo-random source.

It validates the raw entropy with a set of health tests, processes the validated entropy into 384-bit seeds, and makes those seeds available either to a hardware consumer or to software through register reads.

The module also supports:

- FIPS-compliant and bypass operating modes,
- boot-time bypass behavior for early entropy availability,
- firmware override of the normal entropy path,
- recovery alerting when health tests exceed a failure threshold,
- fatal alerting on internal queue or state-machine errors,
- interrupts for entropy availability, health-test failure, and fatal errors.

The module is inactive until explicitly enabled. While disabled, it does not produce entropy outputs and all internal queues are emptied.

---

## 2. Enable and Source Selection

### 2.1 Disabled State

When the module is disabled:

- No entropy samples are collected.
- All internal queues are cleared.
- Health tests are inactive.
- The pseudo-random source is held in a load state and continuously receives the current seed value from the seed register.
- The seed register may be updated, and the new value takes effect when the module is next enabled.

### 2.2 External RNG Source Mode

The module can select an external true-random source. In this mode:

- The module asserts the RNG source enable output.
- Each valid sample supplied by the RNG source is accepted into the entropy pipeline.
- Optional bit-lane mode may be enabled. When enabled, the module selects one bit lane from each raw sample and accumulates the selected bits into 4-bit symbols before health testing. When disabled, the full 4-bit raw sample is used directly.
- The module does not require the RNG source to be paced by the internal rate register; raw full-width samples are consumed as they arrive.

### 2.3 LFSR Source Mode

The module can select the internal pseudo-random LFSR as the entropy source. In this mode:

- The LFSR is loaded from the seed register while the module is disabled.
- Once enabled, the LFSR advances under control of the programmable rate value.
- The RNG source enable output is deasserted unless the external RNG mode is also selected.
- If both source modes are enabled, the LFSR takes priority as the active source for health testing.

### 2.4 Rate Control

The rate register controls the spacing of entropy samples for the LFSR source and for bit-lane collection. A programmed value of zero stops generation in those modes. The module uses the programmed rate to determine when the selected source advances and when a new entropy symbol is presented to the health-test path.

---

## 3. Health Testing

All entropy presented for delivery must pass through the health-test stage. The module supports the following tests:

- Repetition count test
- Adaptive proportion test, with high and low thresholds
- Bucket test
- Markov test, with high and low thresholds
- External vendor health test, when enabled

The internal tests are active unless explicitly disabled. The external test is active only when explicitly enabled.

### 3.1 Test Windows

The module has independently programmable health-test window sizes for:

- normal FIPS mode, and
- bypass mode.

The module selects the window size based on the current operating mode. The window counter advances on each valid entropy symbol. At the end of a window, the windowed tests evaluate their counts and the window counter resets.

The repetition count test is not window-based. It can signal a failure whenever a repeated symbol count reaches its threshold, independent of window boundaries.

### 3.2 Thresholds

Each health test has separate threshold values for FIPS mode and bypass mode. The module selects the active threshold set based on the current operating mode.

Threshold values must be loaded while the module is disabled. Once the module is enabled, the active thresholds remain fixed until the module is disabled and reconfigured.

### 3.3 Health Test Failure Reporting

For each enabled health test, the module maintains:

- a total failure count,
- a watermark value that records the test counter at the time of a failure, and
- a separate alert-oriented fail counter.

Failures from disabled tests must not contribute to any aggregate count.

The module also maintains an aggregate alert fail count that increments whenever any enabled internal or external test reports a failure.

### 3.4 Recovery Alert and Health-Test-Failed Interrupt

The aggregate alert fail count is compared to the programmable alert threshold.

- If the alert threshold is zero, the recovery alert is disabled.
- If the aggregate count reaches a nonzero alert threshold, the module asserts the recovery alert.
- The same event generates the health-test-failed interrupt event.

Alert fail counters are cleared by software via the health-test clear control, and are also cleared by the module when advancing from one health-test window to another, as appropriate.

### 3.5 External Health Test Interface

The module provides the active entropy stream, validity indication, clear control, active control, thresholds, and window size to an external health-test block. It receives back a test count value and high/low failure pulses from that block.

The external test results are included in:

- per-test total fail counters,
- aggregate alert fail counting,
- watermark reporting,
- recovery alert generation.

---

## 4. Entropy Processing

### 4.1 Post-Health Packing

After health testing, the validated entropy symbols are packed into 32-bit words and stored in a pre-condition queue. The depth of this queue is observable through a status register, and the point at which the queue is considered full is programmable.

### 4.2 Normal and Bypass Paths

The module has two paths for producing final 384-bit seeds:

- In normal FIPS mode, entropy from the pre-condition queue is processed through the conditioning stage and packed into 384-bit seeds.
- In bypass mode, entropy from the pre-condition queue is packed directly into 384-bit seeds without passing through the conditioning stage.

Bypass mode is used:

- during boot-bypass operation, and
- when software explicitly selects the bypass processing path.

At reset, the module starts in boot-bypass mode. It automatically leaves boot-bypass mode after the initial seed phase is complete, unless software has disabled boot bypass or explicitly selected bypass mode.

### 4.3 Firmware Override

When firmware override is enabled by both the security enable input and the configuration control, software can take control of the pre-condition queue:

- Software may be selected as the writer to the pre-condition queue, allowing processed entropy to be injected into the pipeline.
- Software may be selected as the reader from the pre-condition queue, allowing raw entropy to be extracted for firmware-side testing or conditioning.
- The current queue fill level is available to software.

If the security enable input is not asserted, firmware override must remain inactive even if the configuration bit is set.

### 4.4 Seed Validity and Fullness

A 384-bit seed must only be released from the processing path if the corresponding health-test window completed successfully.

If a health-test failure occurs for a window, the entropy accumulated for that window must not be delivered as a valid seed.

Complete seeds are stored in the final queue. The fill level of the final queue is observable. If the final queue is full, additional fully processed seeds are dropped until space becomes available.

---

## 5. Entropy Delivery

### 5.1 Hardware Consumer Interface

When delivery to the hardware consumer is selected:

- The module responds to a request only when a seed is available in the final queue.
- When responding, the module presents the 384-bit seed and an associated FIPS compliance flag.
- Hardware delivery is disabled when software delivery is selected; in that configuration, hardware requests must not consume seeds.

The FIPS compliance flag must be asserted only when the seed was produced in normal FIPS mode from the full-width external RNG source, with the LFSR disabled and RNG bit-lane mode disabled. In bypass mode, LFSR mode, or bit-lane mode, the flag must be deasserted.

### 5.2 Software Read Path

When software delivery is selected, complete seeds are unpacked into 32-bit words and made available through the software entropy data register.

The module asserts an entropy-valid interrupt event when at least one 32-bit word is available in the software read path.

Each read of the software entropy data register returns the next 32-bit word and consumes it. A full 384-bit seed requires twelve reads.

The software read path only consumes words when the appropriate security enable input is asserted. If that enable is not asserted, reads must not pop data from the queue.

When software delivery is selected, all available seeds are consumed by the software path and are not delivered to the hardware consumer.

---

## 6. Fatal Error Handling

The module must detect internal protocol violations that indicate a fatal malfunction. These include:

- pushing data into a queue that is already full,
- popping data from a queue that is empty,
- inconsistent queue status conditions,
- an invalid hardware-interface request/acknowledge state, and
- an invalid main processing state.

When a fatal error is detected and the module is enabled:

- the fatal alert output is asserted,
- the fatal error interrupt event is generated, and
- the error code register records the source and type of the error.

A diagnostic error-code test feature allows software to force each error-code bit to be reported. Forced error bits must be treated as valid error sources for reporting and alerting purposes.

---

## 7. Alerts and Interrupts

### 7.1 Recovery Alert

The recovery alert is asserted when the aggregate health-test fail count reaches a nonzero alert threshold. It is not asserted when the threshold is zero.

### 7.2 Fatal Alert

The fatal alert is asserted when a fatal internal error is detected while the module is enabled.

### 7.3 Alert Test Outputs

Dedicated alert test outputs are provided. These outputs assert when software writes the corresponding alert test control bits. They are independent of the normal alert conditions.

### 7.4 Interrupt Events

The module generates interrupt events for:

- entropy data being available in the software read path,
- a health-test failure reaching the recovery alert threshold,
- a fatal internal error.

These events feed the standard interrupt enable, status, and test register logic. The corresponding interrupt outputs must follow standard interrupt behavior, including support for software-triggered interrupt tests.

---

## 8. Reset and Initialization Summary

After reset:

- The module is disabled.
- The module is in boot-bypass mode.
- All queues are empty.
- The pseudo-random source is loaded from the seed register.

To start normal operation, software must:

1. Load the desired seed value while the module is disabled, if using the LFSR source.
2. Configure the rate, health-test thresholds, and windows.
3. Select the desired entropy source mode.
4. Enable the module.

Once enabled, the module continuously collects, tests, conditions, and queues entropy until disabled or reconfigured.
